test_title: English Language and Comprehension Mock Test 10

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.The novel 'The Pearl' stands as a powerful commentary on the dangers of materialism and the importance of embracing values that transcend wealth. Steinbeck’s cautionary tale urges readers to approach life with humility, compassion and a commitment to what truly matters. His exploration of Kino’s journey provides a poignant reminder that while wealth may be alluring, it is often hollow, and that the greatest riches are those rooted in love, integrity and a sense of purpose. Through this story, Steinbeck leaves an enduring legacy, inviting us all to reflect on our own lives and to choose paths that align with our deepest values. Steinbeck crafts a compelling examination of materialism as a force that corrupts individuals and leaves them adrift, cut off from the meaningful aspects of life. Kino’s story is a testament to the dangers of viewing wealth as the ultimate goal, as it often brings with it only illusion, moral compromise and eventual ruin. In the end, it stands as a timeless reminder that while the allure of wealth may be powerful, it is ultimately hollow. Steinbeck leaves with a powerful message: that the true measure of a fulfilling life is not found in wealth or status, but in the strength of our connections with others and the integrity with which we live. True happiness lies not in the pursuit of material gain but in cherishing the intangible yet deeply fulfilling aspects of life: family, integrity and peace.Select the most appropriate title for the passage.
options: Material Success and its Rewards in The Pearl
Kino's Journey: The Struggles of Ambition
An Exploration of Love and Family in Steinbeck's Works
The Hollow Pursuit of Wealth: Lessons from The Pearl
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (The Hollow Pursuit of Wealth: Lessons from The Pearl) है।
